title: RSA Cryptography
subtitle: How RSA works, key sizes, and secure usage

content.text: RSA security is based on the difficulty of factoring large integers. Generating the key pair involves choosing two large primes; breaking RSA requires factoring their product.

content.code:
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa, padding
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes, serialization

private_key = rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)
public_key = private_key.public_key()

# Sign a message
signature = private_key.sign(
    b"Important document",
    padding.PSS(mgf=padding.MGF1(hashes.SHA256()), salt_length=padding.PSS.MAX_LENGTH),
    hashes.SHA256()
)

# Verify (raises if invalid)
public_key.verify(
    signature, b"Important document",
    padding.PSS(mgf=padding.MGF1(hashes.SHA256()), salt_length=padding.PSS.MAX_LENGTH),
    hashes.SHA256()
)
print("Signature valid")

content.text: Use RSA-2048 at minimum. RSA-4096 for long-lived keys. For new systems, prefer ECDSA which is smaller and faster.

questions.question: What is RSA security based on?
options: The difficulty of computing discrete logarithms
The difficulty of factoring large integers
The difficulty of solving elliptic curve equations
The difficulty of inverting hash functions
questions.explanation: RSA is based on the integer factorization problem: it is easy to multiply two large primes but very hard to factor their product.

faq.a: Never implement cryptography yourself. Use a well-audited library like Python's cryptography package. Home-grown crypto is almost always broken.
